# `Locale`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Locale — opaque BCP-47 locale handle for locale-aware text operations.

`Locale.fromTag` is the single constructor; it returns `Nothing` for any
string that is not a structurally valid BCP-47 tag — an invalid tag is a
typed absence, never a silent default.  The locale-aware case functions
(`String.toUpperIn`, `String.toLowerIn`) live on `Ipe.String` and take a
`Locale` produced here.

For the mental model, worked example, and design rationale see the Locales
guide (`ipe doc guide:locale`).

## `Locale`

An opaque, parse-validated BCP-47 locale.

Constructed only via `fromTag`; never a bare string cast.

## `fromTag`

```ipe
fromTag : String -> Maybe Locale
```

`fromTag tag` — attempt to parse `tag` as a BCP-47 language tag.

Returns `Nothing` if the string is not a structurally valid BCP-47 tag.
An invalid tag is always a typed absence, never a silent fallback to a
default locale.

Valid examples: `"en"`, `"tr"`, `"en-US"`, `"zh-Hant-TW"`.

## `toTag`

```ipe
toTag : Locale -> String
```

`toTag locale` — recover the BCP-47 tag string from a `Locale`.
